settings.pluginDesc: Plugins are Go scripts placed in the plugins/ config directory and loaded automatically at startup. Each plugin directory must contain a plugin.go exporting Name and Init.

settings.actionsDesc: Manually trigger a full rescan to refresh all repository statistics.
settings.backupDesc: Take today's local database snapshot right away (stored under backups/ in the data directory). After the first successful snapshot of the day, further manual or automatic backups that day are no-ops.
settings.backupDone: Backup done: {{path}} (a no-op when today's snapshot already exists)
settings.backupCopyHint: Copy each daily local snapshot into a directory you choose (an external drive, a NAS mount, a synced folder all work). Leave it empty = no copies. Every copy is verified before it counts as a copy — a copy you cannot restore is worse than no copy, because it silences the "I have a backup" signal.
settings.backupCopyOk: This directory works: every daily local snapshot is copied here.
settings.backupCopyWillCreate: The directory does not exist yet; it will be created on the first copy.
settings.backupCopyNotConfigured: No off-disk copy directory is configured: the snapshots stay on the disk that holds the data directory.
settings.backupCopyRelativePath: Use an absolute path: a relative path resolves against the process working directory, not the place you meant.
settings.backupCopyNotADirectory: This path is not a directory.
settings.backupCopyUnwritable: This directory cannot be written to; the copy would fail.
settings.backupCopyNoAncestor: No usable parent directory was found; the copy would fail.
settings.backupCopyAncestorUnwritable: This directory cannot be created: the nearest existing parent directory is not writable.
settings.backupCopyStatFailed: This path could not be inspected.
settings.backupCopySameDevice: This directory is on the same disk as the data directory — that is not an off-disk copy: if the disk fails, both copies go with it.
settings.backupRemoteHint: Optional off-site copy: configure an S3-compatible object store (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO on a NAS — all work) and each daily local snapshot is uploaded to your bucket after it is created. Nothing configured = zero egress; only the snapshot copy is ever uploaded, never the live database file.
settings.backupRemoteOff: Remote backup push disabled (no data leaves the machine)
settings.agentClientsDesc: Write Cinder's MCP server into the AI clients' own configuration; after this, those clients can read this project's knowledge base directly. Only the clients you pick and the project directory you pick are touched, and an existing config is backed up as .repotory-init.bak first.
settings.agentClientsHook: Also install the Claude Code session-end handoff hook (writes the handoff note when a session ends)
settings.agentClientsInstructions: Also write the "read context at the start / hand off at the end" instructions into the project's AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (every agent that reads those files will follow them; both files show up in your git changes)
settings.agentClientsScanAfter: Run a scan right after connecting (so the knowledge base is not empty)
settings.agentSetupOk: Connected: the files below were written.
settings.agentSetupBadClient: One of the client names is unknown — nothing was connected.
settings.agentSetupProjectNotFound: That project no longer exists — nothing was connected.
settings.agentSetupVirtualProject: "Uncategorized" is not a real directory and cannot receive client configuration — pick a real project.
settings.agentSetupAutoGroupedProject: That project is an auto-grouped container (your home directory, typically) and cannot receive client configuration — pick a concrete project.
settings.agentSetupMissingDirectory: The project directory is gone or was moved — nothing was connected.
settings.agentSetupBinaryMissing: repotory-mcp was not found on this machine, so there is nothing to register — install it first (or keep it next to Cinder).
settings.agentSetupScanStarted: Connected, and a scan has started.

updates.title: Version updates
updates.desc: Check GitHub Releases for a newer version. The bundle can be downloaded inside the app and verified — but Cinder never replaces itself: once the download finishes it hands the file to the system installer and you decide when to install.
updates.upToDate: You are on the latest version.
updates.autoCheckOnHint: Checks once in the background after launch; a new version is announced in the navigation bar.
updates.autoCheckOffHint: GitHub is contacted only when you click “Check for updates” here.
updates.proxyHint: api.github.com is unreachable on some networks. Set a local proxy (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:7890); leave empty to connect directly.
updates.downloadNote: The download is verified against its SHA256 digest, then the system installer opens. Cinder never replaces the running program.
updates.downloadDoneVerified: Download complete and verified against its SHA256 digest. Choose “Open installer” to continue.
updates.downloadDoneUnverified: Download complete. The release published no digest, so the file could not be verified.
updates.downloadHint: The update can be installed as soon as the download finishes. You can keep using the app in the meantime.
updates.downloadEjected: The installer volume was ejected. Restart Cinder to use the new version.
updates.downloadEjectNone: No mounted installer volume was found.

audit.title: AI call audit and content review
audit.intro: Records the calls this machine makes to an external model (time, endpoint, model, surface, size) and screens prompts against your own rules before they leave. Everything is off by default; with the gates closed behaviour is exactly what it was before.
audit.auditHint: Writes one row per call: time, endpoint, model, surface (MCP / HTTP / desktop), prompt hash and size, review verdict.
audit.outputHint: The head of a streamed reply is already on screen and cannot be recalled; a match only truncates what follows, so the verdict is "flagged" rather than "blocked".
audit.rules: Review rules (one regex per line, # for comments)
audit.rulesHint: You write the rules; Cinder ships no built-in blocklist — keyword matching is a weak control, easy to reword around and easy to misfire on legitimate content. Matching ignores case; a regex that does not compile is skipped and named in the log.
audit.noFullText: Records keep only the prompt’s SHA-256 hash and its size — never the prompt or the reply text — so keys and business data are not written into the same database the knowledge base lives in.
audit.retentionAppendOnly: Audit rows are only ever added, never cleaned up automatically; to remove them, delete the database yourself.
audit.empty: No calls recorded yet. Turn on "Record call audits" and every call to an external model leaves a row here.
